dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5501.text: To send out breath. Formed from 欠 and 口.

shuowen:5502.text: To blow. Another explanation: an impulse to smile. Formed from 欠, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5503.text: To blow warm breath. Formed from 欠, with 虖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5504.text: To blow air. Formed from 欠, with 或 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5505.text: A settled breath. Formed from 欠, with 與 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5506.text: To draw breath inward. Formed from 欠, with 脅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5507.text: To blow air. Formed from 欠, with 賁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5508.text: To rest. Another explanation: breath escaping outward. Formed from 欠, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5509.text: Joy and delight. Formed from 欠, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5510.text: To smile with joy. Formed from 欠, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5511.text: Smiling without disrupting one’s expression is 弞. Formed from 欠, with abbreviated 引 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5512.text: Having a desire in mind. Formed from 欠 and abbreviated 𡪡.

shuowen:5513.text: Fortunate. Formed from 欠, with 气 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the mouth having difficulty speaking.

shuowen:5514.text: Greedy desire. Formed from 欠, with 谷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5515.text: To sing. Formed from 欠, with 哥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5516.text: Drawing breath through the mouth. Formed from 欠, with 耑 indicating the sound. Read like 輇 in 車輇.

shuowen:5517.text: Loathing in the heart, as if about to vomit. Formed from 欠, with 烏 indicating the sound. Another explanation: mouths approaching one another.

shuowen:5518.text: Retching, 歍𣤶. Formed from 欠, with 鼀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5519.text: An anxious appearance. Formed from 欠, with 尗 indicating the sound. Mencius says: “Zeng Xi looked anxious.”

shuowen:5520.text: To hold a smile. Formed from 欠, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5521.text: People laughing at and mocking one another. Formed from 欠, with 虒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5522.text: 歊歊, the appearance of breath issuing. Formed from 欠 and 高; 高 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5523.text: Something being blown up. Formed from 欠, with 炎 indicating the sound. Read like 忽.

shuowen:5524.text: 𣢑𣢑, playful laughter. Formed from 欠, with 之 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5525.text: 钐钐, the appearance of breath issuing. Formed from 欠, with 䍃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5526.text: To chant or whistle. Formed from 欠, with 肅 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “His whistling is song.”

shuowen:5527.text: To chant or sigh. Formed from 欠, with abbreviated 𪅀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5528.text: Sudden joy. Formed from 欠 and 喜.

shuowen:5529.text: To criticize. Formed from 欠, with 矣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5530.text: To vomit. Formed from 欠, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5531.text: To vomit. Formed from 欠, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5532.text: To sigh or sob. Formed from 欠, with 虚 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to exhale.

shuowen:5533.text: To sigh or sob, 歔. Formed from 欠, with abbreviated 稀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5534.text: Vehement anger. Formed from 欠, with 蜀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5535.text: The intention to speak. Formed from 欠 and 𠧴; 𠧴 also indicates the sound. Read like 酉.

shuowen:5536.text: To desire to drink repeatedly. Formed from 欠, with 渴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5537.text: Singing; the preceding 所 in the recorded gloss is uncertain. Formed from 欠, with abbreviated 噭 indicating the sound. Read like 叫 in 叫呼.

shuowen:5538.text: Sorrowful feeling. Formed from 欠, with 嗇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5539.text: To finish the wine. Formed from 欠, with 𥼚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5540.text: A restrained intention: the mouth closed. Formed from 欠, with 緘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5541.text: To point and laugh. Formed from 欠, with 辰 indicating the sound. Read like 蜃.

shuowen:5542.text: 昆干, said to be unknowable; the descriptive phrase is uncertain. Formed from 欠, with 鰥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5543.text: To sip. Formed from 欠, with 臿 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “They sipped the covenant blood and forgot.”

shuowen:5544.text: To suck. Formed from 欠, with 束 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5545.text: To eat without becoming full. Formed from 欠, with 甚 indicating the sound. Read like 坎.

shuowen:5546.text: To desire to obtain. Formed from 欠, with 臽 indicating the sound. Read like 貪.

shuowen:5547.text: To drink. Formed from 欠, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5548.text: Eating without becoming full. Formed from 欠, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5549.text: Breathing obstructed in the throat. Formed from 欠, with 骨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5550.text: To hesitate or murmur, 嚘. Formed from 欠, with 因 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5551.text: Qi moving against its course. Formed from 欠, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5552.text: A sound preceding spitting. Another explanation: a slight smile. Formed from 欠, with 毄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5553.text: To draw in the nose. Formed from 欠, with 翕 indicating the sound. Danyang has She County, 歙.

shuowen:5554.text: To wrinkle or contract the nose. Formed from 欠, with 咎 indicating the sound. The reading is referred to the Erya phrase “麔豭短脰,” “the 麔 boar has a short neck”; the precise reading reference is uncertain.

shuowen:5555.text: A sorrowful appearance. Formed from 欠, with 幼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5556.text: 咄欪, shameless. Another explanation: without inward feeling, 無腸意; the phrase is uncertain. Formed from 欠, with 出 indicating the sound. Read like 卉.

shuowen:5557.text: An explanatory particle. Formed from 欠 and 曰; 曰 also indicates the sound. The Odes says: “Thus seek their peace.”

shuowen:5558.text: Not foremost and not refined. Formed from 欠, with 二 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5559.text: Hungry and empty. Formed from 欠, with 康 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5560.text: To deceive. Formed from 欠, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5561.text: Spirits consuming the vapor of offerings. Formed from 欠, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5562.text: To sing. Formed from 欠, with 俞 indicating the sound. The Qieyun says: “Ba yu means singing.” Note: the Records of the Historian says people of the Yu River excelled in song and dance, and Emperor Gao of Han adopted their music. Later people consequently added this graph.

shuowen:5563.text: To drink. Formed from 欠, with 酓 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 㱃.

shuowen:5564.text: To drink. Formed from abbreviated 㱃, with 叕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5565.text: Mouth fluid from longing and desire. Formed from 欠 and 水. All characters in this group follow 㳄.

shuowen:5566.text: Greedy desire. Formed from 㳄 and abbreviated 羑, the 羑 in 羑呼 and in Youli, 羑里, where King Wen was imprisoned.

shuowen:5567.text: To drink. Formed from 㳄, with 厂 indicating the sound. Read like 移.

shuowen:5568.text: To take things for private advantage. Formed from 㳄, depicting desire for 皿.

shuowen:5569.text: When qi from eating or drinking reverses and one cannot breathe, this is called 㒫. Formed from reversed 欠. All characters in the 㒫 group follow 㒫. Its present clerical transformation is 旡.

shuowen:5570.text: An exclamation of startled aversion. Formed from 㒫, with 咼 indicating the sound. Read like 夥, the Chu term for “many.”

shuowen:5571.text: When affairs are not good, one says 𣄴. The Erya says: “𣄴 means slight.” Formed from 㒫, with 京 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5572.text: The head. Formed from 𦣻 and 几. The ancient graph for bowing the head has this form. All characters in this group follow 頁. 𦣻 is the graph for bowing the head.

shuowen:5573.text: The head. Formed from 頁, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5574.text: The area between the eyebrows and eyes. Formed from 頁, with 彥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5575.text: Appearance. Formed from 頁, with 公 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5576.text: The skull. Formed from 頁, with 乇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5577.text: 𩑒顱, the bones of the head. Formed from 頁, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5578.text: The crown of the head. Formed from 頁, with 𡚇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5579.text: The crown of the head. Formed from 頁, with 眞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5580.text: The crown of the head. Formed from 頁, with 丁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5581.text: The forehead. Formed from 頁, with 桑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5582.text: The forehead. Formed from 頁, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5583.text: The forehead. Formed from 頁, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5584.text: The bridge of the nose. Formed from 頁, with 安 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5585.text: The cheekbones. Formed from 頁, with 𢌳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5586.text: The sides of the face. Formed from 頁, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5587.text: Behind the cheeks. Formed from 頁, with 𥃩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5588.text: The jaw, 𩔞. Formed from 頁, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5589.text: The chin or lower jaw. Formed from 頁, with 圅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5590.text: The stalk supporting the head. Formed from 頁, with 坙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5591.text: The neck. Formed from 頁, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5592.text: The back of the head. Formed from 頁, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5593.text: The nape where the head rests. Formed from 頁, with 冘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5594.text: A protruding forehead. Formed from 頁, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5595.text: A bent or crooked chin. Formed from 頁, with 不 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5596.text: An appearance described as 𪙊, perhaps a gaping or uneven mouth; the gloss is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5597.text: An uneven or crooked face. Formed from 頁, with 尹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5598.text: The head large, 頵頵. Formed from 頁, with 君 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5599.text: A downcast facial appearance, 顚䫟; the phrase is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 員 indicating the sound. Read like 隕.

shuowen:5600.text: A long head and cheeks. Formed from 頁, with 兼 indicating the sound.
